name: George Meyers
bio: George Meyers was a Communist Party and textile-union leader prosecuted under the Smith Act, which made it a crime to advocate the overthrow of the government and was used widely against Communist Party members during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in federal court in Baltimore in April 1952 and sentenced to four years in prison and a $1,000 fine.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Yes — convicted April 1952, federal court, Baltimore
sentence: 4 years in prison and a $1,000 fine

name: Roy Wood
bio: Roy Wood was a Washington, D.C. Communist Party leader prosecuted under the Smith Act, which was used widely against Communist Party members during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in Baltimore in April 1952 and sentenced to three years in prison and a $1,000 fine.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Yes — convicted April 1952, Baltimore
sentence: 3 years in prison and a $1,000 fine

name: Regina Frankfeld
bio: Regina Frankfeld was a Communist Party defendant and the wife of Maryland Communist Party head Phil Frankfeld, prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. She was convicted in Baltimore in April 1952 and sentenced to two years in prison and a $1,000 fine.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Yes — convicted April 1952, Baltimore
sentence: 2 years in prison and a $1,000 fine

name: Ben Dobbs
bio: Ben Dobbs was a Communist Party leader and one of the defendants known as the "Los Angeles 14," prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in federal court in Los Angeles in 1952.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Yes — convicted 1952, federal court, Los Angeles, as one of the "Los Angeles 14"

name: William Allan
bio: William Allan was a Daily Worker correspondent and Communist prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in Detroit in September 1952 and held on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952, Detroit

name: Helen Winter
bio: Helen Winter was a Communist and the wife of convicted Smith Act leader Carl Winter, prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. She was arrested in Detroit in September 1952 and held on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952, Detroit

name: Karly Larsen
bio: Karly Larsen was a union vice-president and Progressive Party figure prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in September 1952 at an International Woodworkers convention.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952 at an International Woodworkers convention

name: William Sentner
bio: William Sentner was a regional leader of the United Electrical Workers (UE) and a Communist prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in St. Louis in September 1952.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952, St. Louis

name: Terry Pettus
bio: Terry Pettus was the editor of the People's World and a Communist prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in Seattle in September 1952.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952, Seattle

name: William Pennock
bio: William Pennock was president of the Washington Pension Union and a Progressive Party figure prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in September 1952 and held on $10,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Awaiting trial — arrested September 1952, Washington state

name: Ben Carreathers
bio: Ben Carreathers was a Black Communist and steelworkers' organizer and one of the defendants known as the "Pittsburgh 6," prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in Pittsburgh in 1951 or 1952.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Arrested 1951–52, Pittsburgh, as one of the "Pittsburgh 6"

name: Irving Weissman
bio: Irving Weissman was a Communist and one of the defendants known as the "Pittsburgh 6," prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was arrested in Pittsburgh in 1951 or 1952.
charges: Smith Act violation (advocating overthrow of the government)
convicted: Arrested 1951–52, Pittsburgh, as one of the "Pittsburgh 6"

name: Hyman Schlessinger
bio: Hyman Schlessinger was a lawyer arrested and tried under Pennsylvania's state sedition law for aiding the defense of Steve Nelson during the McCarthy era. He was prosecuted in Pittsburgh in connection with his legal work on Nelson's defense.
charges: Sedition under the Pennsylvania state sedition law (for aiding Steve Nelson's defense)
convicted: Tried for sedition, Pittsburgh

name: Richard Gladstein
bio: Richard Gladstein was one of the five defense lawyers for the eleven Communist leaders tried at the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial, a landmark McCarthy-era prosecution. He was jailed six months for contempt of court, served his term at Texarkana, and was threatened with disbarment for his courtroom conduct.
charges: Contempt of court (arising from the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial)
convicted: Yes — jailed for contempt of court
sentence: 6 months (served at Texarkana); threatened with disbarment

name: Louis McCabe
bio: Louis McCabe was one of the five defense lawyers for the eleven Communist leaders tried at the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial, a landmark McCarthy-era prosecution. He was cited for contempt of court for his courtroom defense and given a 30-day sentence.
charges: Contempt of court (arising from the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial)
convicted: Yes — cited for contempt of court

name: James MacInnis
bio: James MacInnis was a defense lawyer for labor leader Harry Bridges who was cited for contempt of court during the McCarthy era. The U.S. Supreme Court refused to review his case.
charges: Contempt of court (arising from his defense of Harry Bridges)
convicted: Yes — cited for contempt of court, San Francisco (Supreme Court refused review)

name: Abram Flaxer
bio: Abram Flaxer was president of the United Public Workers union who refused to surrender the union's membership list to the McCarran Senate subcommittee during the McCarthy era. He was prosecuted in Washington, D.C. for contempt of Congress.
charges: Contempt of Congress (refusing to surrender the union's membership list to the McCarran subcommittee)
convicted: Prosecuted for contempt of Congress, Washington, D.C.

name: Mary Jane Keeney
bio: Mary Jane Keeney was a United Nations employee prosecuted for contempt of Congress after the McCarran Committee branded her a Communist during the McCarthy era. Her prosecution in Washington, D.C. was regarded as a test case.
charges: Contempt of Congress (after the McCarran Committee branded her a Communist)
convicted: Prosecuted for contempt of Congress, Washington, D.C. (a test case)

name: Raissa Browder
bio: Raissa Browder was the Russian-born wife of former Communist leader Earl Browder, arrested with him in Yonkers, New York on September 30, 1952 during the McCarthy era. She was charged with perjury concerning her naturalization and jailed when bail was refused after she declined to cooperate.
charges: Perjury (concerning her naturalization)
convicted: Arrested September 30, 1952, Yonkers, NY; jailed when bail was refused

name: J.R. Robertson
bio: J.R. Robertson was an officer of the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) convicted of perjury as a co-defendant and character witness in the Harry Bridges denaturalization-perjury case during the McCarthy era. He was prosecuted in San Francisco.
charges: Perjury (as a co-defendant and character witness in the Harry Bridges case)
convicted: Yes — convicted of perjury, San Francisco

name: Henry Schmidt
bio: Henry Schmidt was an officer of the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) convicted of perjury as a co-defendant and character witness in the Harry Bridges case during the McCarthy era. He was prosecuted in San Francisco.
charges: Perjury (as a co-defendant and character witness in the Harry Bridges case)
convicted: Yes — convicted of perjury, San Francisco

name: William Perl
bio: William Perl was a radical physicist indicted for perjury in connection with the Rosenberg atomic-espionage case during the McCarthy era. He had been jobless since his indictment and was awaiting trial in federal court in New York.
charges: Perjury (in connection with the Rosenberg atomic-espionage case)
convicted: Awaiting trial — indicted, federal court, New York

name: Sidney Weinbaum
bio: Sidney Weinbaum was a Caltech scientist convicted in 1950 in an early Cold War loyalty prosecution for making false statements denying Communist Party membership. He was prosecuted in federal court in California.
charges: False statements / perjury (denying Communist Party membership)
convicted: Yes — convicted 1950, federal court, California

name: Oscar Smilack
bio: Oscar Smilack was cited for contempt of an Ohio un-American activities committee in Columbus after refusing to name his political affiliations during the McCarthy era. He was committed "for observation" to the Lima State Hospital for the criminally insane, where he was held 13 days before being freed on a writ of habeas corpus.
charges: Contempt of an Ohio un-American activities committee (refusing to name his political affiliations)
convicted: Committed "for observation" to the Lima State Hospital; held 13 days, freed on habeas corpus
sentence: 13 days held at the Lima State Hospital; freed on habeas corpus
